senses.sense_definition: The headgear with which a horse is directed, typically consisting of straps, a bit, and reins.

examples.text: She gently slipped the leather <w>bridle</w> over the horse's ears before the morning ride.
The rider pulled lightly on the horse's <w>bridle</w> to steer him back onto the path.

senses.sense_definition: A thing that curbs, restrains, or controls.

examples.text: Strict financial regulations act as an effective <w>bridle</w> on excessive corporate risk.
He believed that moral education served as a necessary <w>bridle</w> upon selfish impulses.

senses.sense_definition: A length of cable, rope, or chain attached to two points to distribute a pull or load.

examples.text: The crew secured the towing <w>bridle</w> to both sides of the barge before starting the engine.
He adjusted the kite's <w>bridle</w> lines to improve its stability in high winds.

senses.sense_definition: A heavy mooring cable or hawser used to secure a vessel.

examples.text: The ship was anchored firmly to the harbor buoy using a heavy steel <w>bridle</w>.
Inspect the mooring <w>bridle</w> regularly to ensure the hawser has not frayed under tension.

senses.sense_definition: A small internal plate in a gunlock that keeps the tumbler and sear in position.

examples.text: The gunsmith carefully cleaned the antique lock and lubricated the small <w>bridle</w>.
Without the <w>bridle</w> holding the tumbler secure, the firing mechanism would fail.

senses.sense_definition: A gesture of lifting the head and pulling in the chin to express pride, indignation, or vanity.

examples.text: With an indignant <w>bridle</w>, she dismissed the critical comment and turned away.
His pompous manner was obvious in every haughty <w>bridle</w> and haughty glance.

senses.sense_definition: To show anger, resentment, or offence, especially in response to a slight or suggestion.

examples.text: Several members of the committee <w>bridled</w> at the suggestion that they had acted unfairly.
She visibly <w>bridled</w> when her colleague questioned her professional credentials.

senses.sense_definition: To fit a bridle onto an animal.

examples.text: The stablehand helped the young rider to saddle and <w>bridle</w> the pony.
He learned how to <w>bridle</w> his mare calmly every morning before training.

senses.sense_definition: To restrain, curb, or control, especially one's speech, emotions, or passions.

examples.text: He struggled to <w>bridle</w> his anger during the tense negotiation.
You must learn to <w>bridle</w> your tongue when speaking to your elders.

senses.sense_definition: To hold one's head high and draw in the chin to display pride, vanity, or disdain.

examples.text: She <w>bridled</w> proudly as the crowd applauded her performance.
Offended by the remark, he drew himself up and <w>bridled</w> with visible disdain.
